explanation: Retrospective feature of interpretive commentary rather than procedure or description: the pole fires on the words a text uses to construe, discuss or evaluate a subject - the commentary verbs (discuss, describe, suggest, recommend, highlight, explain, evaluate, assess, examine, refer, indicate, mean) and the construal nouns that name what a discussion, an argument or a guide is made of (aspect, factor, framework, principle, theme, statement, view, perspective, approach, reason, way, means, tip, step, advice, overview, variety, assumption, concern), plus the prepositions that bind them to their complement (about, regarding, concerning) and 'how' - and it stays at or below about 0.2 on the vocabulary of procedure and observation (measure, test, record, observe, find; data, evidence, results, method, process, system, problem, example, theory, analysis, study), on concrete entities and substances (table, metal, river, bread, soil, alloy), on physical actions (run, eat, cut, weigh, carry, dig), on quantities and units, and on personal or narrative deixis (the, a, he, she, we, they, my, then, now, later). Because the pole reads a token with little left context as a bare token, a text's first position (and often its second) also fires on roughly a third of the vocabulary - A/An, this/these, several/both/all/each, when/while/if/however/although, what/how/why - so its inactivity predictions hold for a word that has a clause of running text before it.
